title: A More Stable(coin) Path To The Moon
body_text: A More Stable(coin) Path To The Moon Sablecoins? You mean Bitcoin? Cryptocurrencies are a type of digital money you can send online. As opposed to traditional currency, there is no government issuing crypto and no financial institution facilitating each transaction of crypto. Given its decentralized nature, crypto offers a new, faster way of handling money that can work across borders that can keep working even if one institution fails. The most well-known cryptocurrency, and most widely-used for transactions, is Bitcoin. However, cryptocurrencies can have wild price swings, making them hard to use for everyday spending. Stablecoins are a type of cryptocurrency, but they’re different from coins like Bitcoin because their price doesn’t jump up and down all the time. Instead, they are designed to stay at a steady value (usually $1 per coin). To make that possible, each stablecoin is tied (or “pegged”) to the US dollar or other financial assets. In practice, stablecoins work using a mint-and-redeem mechanism: If someone gives a stablecoin company 1 real US dollar, the company creates (or mints) 1 new stablecoin for that person. Later, if that person wants their real dollar back, the company takes away (or burns) the stablecoin and returns $1 from the money it has saved. Because of this system, stablecoins can act like digital dollars you can send instantly: useful for buying things, sending money to friends or using in crypto apps without worrying about big price swings. The 2 biggest stablecoins — Tether (USDT) and Circle’s USD Coin (USDC) — make up about 93% of all stablecoins in the world, and both are backed by the US dollar. A Stellar Record From January to July 2025, transaction volume, that is, the total amount of money moved using stablecoins, rose 83% compared to last year, reaching over five trillion dollars. Some of this activity comes from computers automatically trading back and forth extremely fast, but even if you remove that, regular everyday use still adds up to about one trillion dollars — more than double last year. Source: McKinsey The balance of stablecoins in circulation, which is the amount of stablecoins actually held out there, has also grown fast. In August 2024, there were about $159 billion worth of stablecoins in use. By August 2025, that number jumped to $250 billion, with most of that coming from the two biggest stablecoins: USDT and USDC. During this same time, about 30% of all crypto transactions involved stablecoins, showing that they are becoming one of the main ways people move money around in digital markets. While stablecoins have already seen tremendous growth, there are three trends for stablecoins that have recently kicked off which warrant the attention of retail investors. All of them surround a massive integration shift: integration into global payments, institutional finance and even US Treasury markets. More Countries, More Money The biggest driver of stablecoins is globalization. As the world’s economy is more connected than ever, demand rises for a fast, cheap way to send money across borders — a demand stablecoins satisfy. Normal international payments (like wiring money overseas) can take several days to arrive, charge high fees, especially foreign exchange (FX) fees and use complicated banking systems like SWIFT. Stablecoins are different: you can send them in minutes, and the fee is often less than 1%. A great example is remittances , that is, money that overseas workers send back home to support family. These transfers often cost over 6% in fees using traditional services. With stablecoins, people can send money almost instantly for far cheaper. For workers in the US sending money to Mexico specifically, stablecoins already make up 5-10% of all transfers, and experts think they may reach 30% within 3-5 years. Stablecoins are also growing because the world relies heavily on the US dollar, which is the main currency used for global trade. Right now, about $15 trillion worth of US dollars are used outside the United States — a number that will likely increase as international trade and financial markets grow with more globalization. In many developing countries, it’s hard to access actual dollars or open a dollar bank account. But stablecoins like USDT and USDC are easy to get on crypto exchanges and apps. So people in places like Argentina (in 2023) used stablecoins as a safe, digital replacement for dollars when their local currency was unstable. A Friend of Uncle Sam Another driver of stablecoins is because financial institutions are embracing them. Earlier this year, the GENIUS Act was passed, which set clear rules to make stablecoins safer: most importantly requiring real dollar backing, liquidity standards and transparency. The newfound reliability and ensuing optimisms leads many people to believe the stablecoin market could grow massively and even be worth over three trillion dollars by 2030. Stablecoins are especially becoming popular for business-to-business (B2B) payments Since early 2025, B2B stablecoin payments have grown 113% , and they now make up about two-thirds of all stablecoin activity. Big banks are also getting involved. Many leaders in finance say they already use stablecoins or expect to within the next three years, and global institutions are building their own stablecoin plans. A group of 10 major banks — including Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs and UBS — is exploring a multi-currency stablecoin. Meanwhile, 9 European banks are working on a euro-based stablecoin built on regulated systems. All of this shows that stablecoins are no longer just a niche crypto idea. Instead, they’re becoming part of the everyday financial system, used by real banks and companies around the world. Credibility by Osmosis Stablecoins aren’t just popular with users but are also becoming deeply connected to other parts of the macroeconomy, especially the US government debt (Treasury) market. Companies that issue major stablecoins, like Tether and Circle, keep back over 80% of their reserves with short-term US Treasuries, becoming critical buyers of US government bonds. By the end of 2024, Tether alone owned about $94.5 billion worth of US Treasuries, which is close to 1% of all US debt held by foreign countries. From early 2024 to early 2025, stablecoins as a whole became the third-largest buyers of US Treasuries, with only the Cayman Islands and Belgium buying more. If stablecoin growth continues, they could soon become a key source of funding for the US government. Stablecoin issuers' role in the US Treasury market means stablecoins are gaining more legitimacy and importance, thereby giving regulators, investors and financial institutions even more reason to support them as they continue to expand. Source: Brookings Institution What to Consider The above trends show how stablecoins are moving into the spotlight, away from being simply a speculative crypto niche. As regulation matures, cross-border adoption accelerates, and multinational firms increasingly integrate stablecoins into payments, the entire stablecoin ecosystem — issuers, exchanges, fintechs, banks, remittance companies and liquidity providers — should be considered by retail investors. title: Why Adhesive Selection Matters for Rigid Packaging Efficiency
summary: Discover how the right rigid packaging adhesive improves sealing strength, machine uptime, and cost efficiency. Learn best practices from H.B. Fuller experts.
body_text: In today’s high-speed manufacturing environments, adhesive selection plays a critical role in rigid packaging efficiency. Beyond simply bonding packs, the right adhesive directly impacts seal strength, machine uptime, operational reliability, and total cost of ownership. At H.B. Fuller, industry-leading brands such as Advantra®, Swift®tak and Swift®melt are engineered to support rigid packaging manufacturers in achieving consistent better operational efficiency across demanding end-of-line operations. How the Right Adhesive Improves Sealing Strength in Rigid Packaging Reliable sealing is essential to protect products throughout transportation, warehousing, and retail handling. Poor adhesive performance can result in seal failures, leaks, or damaged packs—leading too costly rework and brand risk. The right adhesive helps: Maintain pack integrity during distribution and storage Prevent leakage, contamination, or tampering Support heavy or high-value rigid packs across substrates like plastic, metal, glass, and coated paperboard Selecting an adhesive engineered for the specific packaging format and operating conditions is critical to achieving strong, reliable seals throughout the product lifecycle. Adhesive Selection and Machine Uptime in End-of-Line Operations Adhesive-related issues can be a cause of unplanned downtime in rigid packaging and case sealing lines. Problems such as stringing, charring, poor open-time control, or inconsistent viscosity can interrupt packaging line operations and reduce throughput. Choosing the right adhesive can: Enable clean, consistent application at high seed lines Reduce nozzle clogging and equipment fouling Improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) through stable performance Adhesives engineered for thermal stability, controlled viscosity, and long pot life help minimize maintenance interventions and support sustained, efficient end-of-line operations. Adhesive Value Beyond Price While adhesive cost is often evaluated on a per-kilogram basis, the true cost lies in total system efficiency. Performance-driven adhesive selection can significantly reduce operational expenses. According to packaging industry studies, improving adhesive efficiency can lead to measurable savings in materials, maintenance, and downtime costs. Avoiding Common Adhesive-Related Issues in End-of-Line Packaging Drawing on real-world packaging line experience, H.B. Fuller recommends the following best practices for rigid packaging operations: 1. Match Adhesive Chemistry to the Application Different substrates and pack weights require specific adhesive formulations, such as metallocene-based hot melts or specialty solutions. 2. Optimize Application Temperatures Operating adhesives outside recommended temperature ranges can cause stringing, charring, or weak bonds. 3. Select the Right Open and Set Time High-speed rigid packaging lines require adhesives that balance adequate open time with fast setting for downstream handling. 4. Maintain Clean Application Equipment Routine cleaning of tanks, hoses, and nozzles prevents buildup that can compromise adhesive flow and bond consistency. 5. Validate Performance Through Line Trials Conducting real production trials ensures adhesives perform reliably under actual operating conditions. The H.B. Fuller Advantage in Rigid Packaging Adhesives With trusted brands such as Advantra® and Swift®, H.B. Fuller combines advanced adhesive technology, deep application expertise, and hands-on technical support to help rigid packaging manufacturers optimize end-of-line performance. By focusing on stronger seals, higher machine uptime, and lower total cost of ownership, H.B. Fuller enables customers to turn adhesive selection into a long-term competitive advantage.

title: 62% of respondents cite data sovereignty and privacy risks as the biggest factor slowing AI projects in the public cloud
summary: New survey findings to be unveiled at MWC Barcelona 2026 show sovereignty and privacy risks are now the top barriers to AI adoption for…...
body_text: 62% of respondents cite data sovereignty and privacy risks as the biggest factor slowing AI projects in the public cloud February 26, 2026 9:00 am EST Download as PDF New survey findings to be unveiled at MWC Barcelona 2026 show sovereignty and privacy risks are now the top barriers to AI adoption for network protection LONDON, Feb. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Data sovereignty is fast becoming make or break for AI-driven network safety projects. Yet new survey data shows that one in six organisations cannot rely on access to facilities with guaranteed data sovereignty, while data sovereignty and privacy risks are cited as the leading factor slowing AI projects in the public cloud. These are the findings of research sponsored by Arqit (Nasdaq: ARQQ, ARQQW) and Intel that are set to be unveiled at MWC Barcelona 2026. As operators and enterprises push AI deeper into network operations, security teams are being asked to both move faster against escalating threats and ensure sensitive data remains under sovereign control. The latter is becoming more challenging as AI pipelines span public cloud, private infrastructure and edge locations. The result is a growing gap between ambition and practical execution. The research which included a survey of Mobile World Live (MWL) readers found that data sovereignty has now become a project gating issue. 62% of respondents cite data sovereignty and privacy risks as the biggest factor slowing AI projects in the public cloud. More starkly, one in six (16%) say they have no access to facilities with guaranteed data sovereignty at all, underlining how quickly sovereignty has become king for data security. Key findings include: 62% cite data sovereignty and privacy risks as the biggest factor slowing AI projects when using a public cloud. 69% say leveraging AI for network safety is urgent or very important, yet 60% are still testing AI for network security or have not deployed it. 80% expect to use confidential computing to achieve data sovereignty in cloud or edge locations in the next 12 months, including 41% planning deployments across both cloud and edge. 16% say they have no access to facilities with guaranteed data sovereignty, and only 8% say they have guaranteed sovereignty at the edge. Delays to AI transformation are already being felt as operational pain, with impacts on operational efficiency (53%), competitive advantage (48%) and customer experience (45%). These findings come at a moment when AI and automation are becoming central to the connectivity industry’s roadmap. AI can help defenders detect anomalies and harden networks at scale, but it also increases the volume, sensitivity and movement of data. Training and operating models often requires sharing telemetry, logs and security signals between various stakeholders and platforms, making sovereignty constraints harder to ignore. “AI is quickly becoming part of the network security stack, but the data feeding those systems is among the most sensitive that operators and critical infrastructure providers hold,” says Andy Leaver, CEO of Arqit. “This research with MWL shows sovereignty is now a make-or-break requirement, with the majority of teams citing sovereignty and privacy risks as the biggest brake on AI projects in the public cloud. “At the same time, one in six organisations tell us they cannot guarantee sovereign facilities at all, and only 8% can rely on sovereign edge environments today. That gap is exactly where security leaders need stronger controls for data in transit, better visibility into cryptographies, and a practical means of building trust across cloud and edge.” Arqit’s work with telecoms and network operators focuses on protecting data in motion across complex, distributed environments. At MWC 2026, Arqit is demonstrating how operators can move faster on network security without losing control of sensitive data as AI workflows expand across public cloud, private infrastructure and edge locations. On Stand 7C11 in Hall 7 in the UK Pavilion , Arqit and Intel will showcase how they are working together to help organisations benefit safely from AI-assisted network safety, and provide genuine, end-to-end sovereignty for enterprise customers. ©Intel, the Intel logo and other Intel marks are trademarks of Intel Corporation or its subsidiaries. title: Safepay Raast is now generally available

body_text: All posts Blog Safepay Raast is now generally available Raast on Safepay is now generally available, bringing real-time bank transfers into your existing Safepay integration with reliable webhooks, reconciliation, and operational tooling. Ziyad Parekh @ziyadparekh Safepay Raast is now generally available When payments work best, they feel effortless — almost invisible. A customer taps “Pay,” funds move instantly, and confirmation arrives before the moment has time to feel uncertain. But real-world payments aren’t always that simple. Bank rails can introduce delays, integrations can be complex, and reliability across institutions can vary. For businesses operating in Pakistan, this has historically meant balancing speed, cost, and operational complexity when accepting bank payments. Today, we’re excited to announce that Raast on Safepay is now generally available (GA) . Raast brings Pakistan’s instant payment infrastructure directly into the Safepay platform, enabling merchants and fintechs to accept real-time bank transfers with the same developer experience, reliability, and operational tooling they already expect from Safepay. What started as early integrations with pilot customers has evolved into a production-grade payment rail — one that gives businesses the speed, control, and cost efficiency they need to scale. You can explore the full integration guides in our documentation: https://safepay.mintlify.app Real-time payments, built into your existing Safepay stack Raast is Pakistan’s instant payment system operated by the State Bank of Pakistan. It enables immediate interbank transfers using aliases such as mobile numbers, IBANs, or Raast IDs. With general availability, Raast becomes a first-class payment method inside Safepay , alongside cards and wallets. Merchants can now: Accept instant bank payments with real-time confirmation Reduce payment costs compared to card rails Improve conversion for customers who prefer bank transfers Reconcile payments automatically through Safepay APIs and webhooks All of this happens without requiring merchants to build or maintain direct bank integrations. The goal is simple: one integration, multiple payment rails. Designed for reliability and operational scale Since the initial rollout, we’ve focused heavily on production readiness — especially around reliability, observability, and reconciliation. Raast payments on Safepay now include: Real-time payment state tracking Payment lifecycle events are delivered through the same webhook system merchants already use for cards, making operational handling consistent across rails. Automatic reconciliation and settlement visibility Transactions flow through Safepay’s reporting and settlement systems, eliminating manual matching between bank statements and payment records. Robust retry and failure handling Edge cases such as delayed confirmations, bank timeouts, or customer interruptions are handled gracefully, reducing operational burden for merchants. Together, these improvements deliver a payment experience that feels as predictable as cards — while retaining the cost and speed advantages of bank transfers. A better option for high-trust and high-value payments In many industries, customers prefer bank payments over cards — especially for: Education and tuition payments Travel and ticketing E-commerce with higher ticket sizes Government and utility payments Marketplace payouts and collections Raast provides a native solution for these use cases. Because payments settle instantly and irrevocably, merchants benefit from: Immediate payment confirmation Lower fraud risk compared to cards Improved cash-flow timing Reduced chargeback exposure For many businesses, Raast becomes not just an alternative payment method — but the primary rail . Built for developers One of Safepay’s core principles is that new payment methods should not require new complexity. Raast follows the same API patterns as the rest of the platform: Create a payment intent Present payment instructions to the customer Receive confirmation via webhook Reconcile through dashboards and reports If you’ve integrated Safepay before, you already know how to use Raast. Full developer documentation is available here: https://safepay.mintlify.app Observability and control from day one General availability also introduces deeper visibility into Raast transactions. Merchants can monitor: Payment status transitions in real time Settlement and reconciliation data Failure and exception cases Customer payment behavior patterns This removes much of the operational guesswork that typically comes with bank transfer integrations. When issues arise, it’s easy to determine what happened, why it happened, and what action — if any — is required. A core building block for Pakistan’s digital payments future With GA, Raast becomes a foundational part of Safepay’s payment infrastructure. It enables: Instant bank payments at national scale Lower acceptance costs compared to cards Real-time settlement visibility Unified payment orchestration across rails Most importantly, it does this without compromising Safepay’s core guarantees: reliability, security, and a clean developer experience. Getting started Raast is now available to Safepay merchants. Integration is straightforward and can be enabled alongside your existing payment methods with minimal changes. You can deploy incrementally, test in staging environments, and roll out to production at your own pace. To begin, visit our documentation: https://safepay.mintlify.app If you need onboarding support or have specific volume requirements, our team is ready to help. Instant payments are no longer the future of Pakistan — they’re here now. And with Safepay, they’re ready to use.

title: Xero vs QuickBooks vs FreshBooks
body_text: Choosing the right accounting software stands as one of the most critical decisions for your business's financial management strategy. The market offers numerous options with varying features, pricing models, and user experiences that can significantly impact your daily operations. Accounting software serves as the backbone of your financial infrastructure, helping you track expenses, manage invoices, and generate reports that guide important business decisions. How Do These Accounting Platforms Compare? Modern accounting solutions offer far more than basic bookkeeping capabilities, transforming into comprehensive financial management systems. Each platform brings unique strengths to the table, catering to different business sizes, industries, and accounting needs. Understanding these differences helps you select the solution that aligns perfectly with your specific requirements. The right accounting software should grow with your business, adapting to changing needs while maintaining ease of use. Many entrepreneurs find themselves switching platforms as they scale, often discovering that what worked for a freelance operation becomes insufficient for a growing company with multiple employees and more complex financial tracking needs. The Core Players in Small Business Accounting QuickBooks represents one of the most established and versatile accounting systems available today. This robust platform offers both desktop and cloud-based solutions packed with features designed to handle comprehensive accounting needs across various business sizes. The software excels in providing detailed reporting options, extensive user customization, and a wide range of integrations that make it suitable for established small and medium-sized businesses requiring sophisticated financial management. Xero has emerged as a powerful cloud-based accounting solution known for its modern, user-friendly design coupled with extensive functionality. Small businesses particularly appreciate its streamlined bank reconciliation processes, multi-currency support, and vast integration ecosystem. While users might experience a steeper initial learning curve, Xero's flexibility allows it to scale alongside growing businesses, especially those requiring seamless integration with payment processors and third-party applications. FreshBooks began as a specialized invoicing solution primarily targeting freelancers and micro-businesses. This cloud-based platform focuses on delivering intuitive invoicing, expense tracking, and time management tools without overwhelming users with unnecessary complexity. Though it may lack some advanced features found in full-scale accounting systems, FreshBooks wins praise for its straightforward interface and simplified user experience that allows business owners to manage financial tasks efficiently. What Makes These Platforms User-Friendly? The usability of accounting software directly impacts your productivity and financial management efficiency. An intuitive interface reduces the learning curve, minimizes errors, and ensures you can access critical financial information quickly when making business decisions. Each platform approaches user experience differently, balancing simplicity against functionality. Your choice should reflect your technical comfort level, the complexity of your financial needs, and how much time you can dedicate to learning a new system. How FreshBooks Simplifies Financial Management FreshBooks prioritizes simplicity with a clean, inviting interface featuring straightforward navigation. This design philosophy makes creating invoices, tracking time, and monitoring expenses remarkably intuitive, even for users with no accounting background. The platform's approach removes intimidation from financial management tasks. The onboarding experience includes helpful walkthroughs that guide new users through essential functions step by step. This structured introduction helps businesses start using the platform productively within minutes rather than hours or days. The guided setup ensures you can begin invoicing clients and tracking expenses immediately. FreshBooks offers an exceptional mobile experience through its well-designed app. The mobile interface maintains functionality without feeling cramped, allowing users to create professional invoices and track work while away from their desks. This mobility proves invaluable for service-based businesses whose owners frequently work on client sites or travel between locations. Why QuickBooks Balances Power With Accessibility QuickBooks strikes a balance between robust functionality and user accessibility. The interface presents more complexity than FreshBooks but includes customization options that help both beginners and advanced users navigate the system efficiently. This flexibility allows the platform to serve diverse business needs without overwhelming new users. Users can personalize their dashboard experience by: Highlighting frequently used features for quick access Hiding rarely used functions to reduce visual clutter Creating custom shortcuts to streamline common workflows Setting up automated reports based on specific business metrics QuickBooks requires a moderate learning investment compared to simpler platforms. The extensive feature set means new users typically need several hours to fully explore and understand the software's capabilities. However, this initial time investment pays dividends through powerful financial management tools that support complex business operations. How Xero Delivers Advanced Features With Modern Design Xero presents a feature-rich interface that might initially appear dense due to its comprehensive functionality. The dashboard contains numerous options and built-in reports that provide immediate financial insights. This wealth of information creates initial complexity but delivers significant value for businesses needing detailed financial management. The platform offers excellent migration support for businesses transitioning from other accounting systems. Free migration services and detailed guides help users transfer existing financial data without disrupting operations. This support minimizes downtime during the switch to Xero and preserves historical financial records. Frequent users quickly appreciate Xero's advanced capabilities that streamline complex financial processes. The learning curve flattens considerably after the initial orientation period, revealing a powerful system that handles sophisticated accounting needs while maintaining reasonable usability. The platform rewards persistence with exceptional financial management capabilities. How Do Invoicing Capabilities Compare? Invoicing represents one of the most frequently used functions in accounting software, directly impacting your cash flow and client relationships. Effective invoicing systems should create professional documents quickly, track payment status automatically, and offer flexible payment options for your customers. The right invoicing solution balances professional presentation with payment convenience, helping you get paid faster while maintaining a polished business image. Consider how each platform handles recurring invoices, customization options, and payment processing when making your selection. FreshBooks Invoicing Features That Save Time FreshBooks excels in creating professional invoices through an intuitive process requiring minimal clicks. The streamlined workflow guides users through each step, from client selection to payment terms, ensuring nothing important gets overlooked. This efficiency particularly benefits businesses that send numerous invoices regularly. The platform offers these personalization options for invoices: Custom logo placement for brand consistency Adjustable layouts to highlight important information Recurring invoice scheduling for subscription-based services Automated payment reminders to improve collection rates FreshBooks supports multiple payment methods including credit cards, bank transfers, and digital wallets. This flexibility improves client convenience and accelerates payment collection. The system automatically records payments against outstanding invoices, eliminating manual reconciliation work and providing clear visibility into accounts receivable status. QuickBooks Advanced Invoicing Capabilities QuickBooks provides extensive invoice customization options beyond basic branding. Users can create detailed line-item customizations, add product images, and include specific terms and conditions tailored to each client relationship. This flexibility helps businesses present professional, comprehensive invoices that clearly communicate value delivered. The platform integrates mobile payment solutions through QuickBooks GoPayment service, enabling businesses to accept credit card payments in person using mobile card readers. This feature proves particularly valuable for businesses combining physical locations with remote services or those conducting sales at events, trade shows, or client sites. QuickBooks offers a comprehensive dashboard that displays real-time insights into invoice status, payment trends, and overdue accounts. This visibility helps businesses proactively manage cash flow by identifying payment delays early and taking appropriate follow-up actions. The system also generates aging reports that highlight which clients consistently pay late. Xero's Comprehensive Invoicing System Xero stands out by offering more than 15 professional invoice templates, providing exceptional customization flexibility. These diverse options allow businesses to create industry-specific invoices that align perfectly with their brand identity and communication style. The template variety ensures invoices look professional across different business contexts. The platform excels in automation through: Recurring invoice scheduling with flexible frequency options Approval workflows that ensure accuracy before sending Automatic payment reminders at customizable intervals Instant payment status updates when clients view invoices Xero integrates seamlessly with inventory management systems and third-party applications, creating an efficient workflow that reduces manual data entry. This integration automatically updates inventory levels when invoicing for physical products and synchronizes with shipping systems to streamline order fulfillment processes. What Reporting Tools Do These Platforms Offer? Financial reporting provides the insights needed for informed business decisions. Effective reporting tools should present clear financial snapshots, identify trends, and highlight areas requiring attention. The depth and customization of these reports vary significantly between platforms. Consider how each system balances report complexity against usability, especially if you lack extensive accounting knowledge. The ideal reporting solution should provide actionable insights without requiring advanced financial expertise to interpret the data. FreshBooks Reporting for Quick Financial Insights FreshBooks delivers straightforward visual reports focusing on essential metrics like revenue streams, outstanding payments, expense categories, and profit margins. These easy-to-interpret graphics provide immediate financial clarity without overwhelming users with excessive detail. The simplified approach makes financial monitoring accessible even for those without accounting backgrounds. Reports can be quickly exported as PDF or Excel files with a few clicks. This export flexibility facilitates sharing financial information with team members, accountants, or other stakeholders who might need access to your business data. The portable format ensures compatibility across different systems and allows for additional analysis using specialized tools. FreshBooks reporting works best for businesses needing quick financial snapshots rather than complex analysis. The platform prioritizes clarity over depth, making it ideal for freelancers and small businesses with straightforward financial structures. The system provides sufficient insights for basic business planning without the complexity of more advanced reporting systems. QuickBooks Comprehensive Reporting Capabilities QuickBooks offers over 80 built-in reports covering every aspect of business finances. These pre-configured reports address standard business needs while custom report options allow users to create specialized analyses for unique requirements. This extensive library ensures businesses can monitor performance across multiple dimensions simultaneously. The platform automatically generates critical financial statements including: Detailed balance sheets showing assets and liabilities Profit and loss statements with customizable date ranges Cash flow statements tracking money movement Sales tax reports for compliance requirements QuickBooks enhances reporting usability through customizable dashboards and advanced search functions. Users can drill down into transaction details directly from summary reports, allowing for quick investigation of unusual patterns or discrepancies. This seamless navigation between summary and detail views streamlines financial analysis and problem-solving. Xero's Interactive Reporting Dashboard Xero features real-time interactive dashboards that display financial metrics through engaging visual representations. These dynamic interfaces allow users to adjust parameters instantly and see how changes affect different aspects of business performance. The interactive approach transforms passive report viewing into active financial exploration. While Xero's downloadable reports might appear more basic than QuickBooks offerings, the platform compensates through exceptional drill-down capabilities. Users can click on any dashboard element to reveal supporting transactions and detailed breakdowns. This interactive functionality often provides more practical value than static reports by encouraging deeper financial understanding. The platform particularly excels in supporting businesses managing multiple entities. Consolidated reporting options allow users to view combined financial performance across different business units while maintaining the ability to examine each entity individually. This multi-level visibility proves invaluable for businesses with complex organizational structures. How Much Do These Platforms Cost? Pricing represents a crucial consideration when selecting accounting software. The right balance between cost and functionality ensures you get necessary features without paying for capabilities you won't use. Each platform offers tiered pricing models designed to accommodate different business sizes and needs. Consider not just current costs but how pricing scales as your business grows. Additional users, advanced features, and increased transaction volumes can significantly impact monthly expenses over time. Look beyond the initial price point to understand the total cost of ownership. FreshBooks Pricing Structure Explained FreshBooks employs a tiered pricing model with plans tailored to different client volumes. The Lite plan costs approximately £15 monthly and accommodates up to five billable clients, making it ideal for freelancers or businesses with a small client base. This entry-level option provides core invoicing and expense tracking functionality at an accessible price point. As your client roster expands, you can upgrade to the Plus plan (around £25 monthly) or Premium plan (approximately £35 monthly) to accommodate larger client volumes. These higher tiers also introduce additional features like double-entry accounting reports and project profitability tracking that support more complex business operations. FreshBooks offers excellent value for businesses primarily needing invoicing and time-tracking capabilities. However, lower-tier plans lack comprehensive features like full bank reconciliation or complete financial statements that growing businesses might eventually require. Consider your anticipated future needs when evaluating the platform's long-term value proposition. QuickBooks Pricing Options for Different Business Sizes QuickBooks Online provides multiple subscription tiers including Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, and Advanced. A specialized Self-Employed version caters specifically to freelancers at a lower price point. This diverse pricing structure allows businesses to select the exact feature set they need without overpaying for unnecessary capabilities. The platform's scalability allows seamless transitions between plans as your business grows. Upgrading unlocks additional features and user access, though monthly costs increase accordingly. This progressive approach ensures businesses can start with basic functionality and expand their accounting capabilities alongside business growth. When evaluating QuickBooks pricing, consider factors beyond the monthly subscription fee. Additional costs may apply for multiple user access, advanced inventory tracking, or specialized industry features. These supplementary expenses can significantly impact the total cost of ownership, especially for growing businesses with evolving needs. Xero's Value-Based Pricing Approach Xero offers three primary plans: Starter, Standard, and Premium, with the Starter plan beginning around £15 monthly. This straightforward pricing structure makes budget planning simple and predictable. The transparent approach eliminates confusion about what features come with each tier. One of Xero's most compelling advantages is unlimited user access across all pricing plans. This unique benefit allows growing businesses to add team members, accountants, or advisors without incurring additional per-user fees. The unlimited access model can deliver substantial cost savings for businesses with multiple financial stakeholders. Xero provides optional add-on features such as payroll processing and project tracking available for separate fees. This modular approach allows businesses to customize their accounting solution by selecting only the additional capabilities they genuinely need. The flexibility prevents overpaying for bundled features that might go unused in other platforms. Which Platform Offers Better Integrations? Integration capabilities significantly impact accounting software utility by connecting financial data with other business systems. Strong integration ecosystems eliminate duplicate data entry, reduce errors, and create comprehensive business management solutions that extend beyond basic accounting. Consider which other business tools you currently use or plan to implement when evaluating integration options. The ideal accounting platform should connect seamlessly with your existing technology stack while providing flexibility for future additions. FreshBooks Integration Ecosystem FreshBooks connects with over 100 third-party applications spanning marketing tools, payment processors, and customer relationship management systems. This integration network allows small businesses to create efficient workflows that eliminate redundant data entry and maintain consistency across platforms. These integrations enable powerful automation capabilities: Automatic invoice creation when projects complete in project management tools Direct expense import from connected bank accounts and credit cards Seamless time tracking synchronization with productivity applications Instant payment recording when clients use integrated payment processors The platform's integration approach focuses on quality over quantity, ensuring each connected application works reliably rather than offering numerous unstable connections. This curated ecosystem provides sufficient options for most small businesses while maintaining simplicity and dependability. QuickBooks Extensive Integration Network QuickBooks leads the market with over 750 app integrations covering virtually every business function. This extensive ecosystem allows businesses to connect their accounting system with specialized tools for industry-specific needs, creating comprehensive business management solutions tailored to unique requirements. The platform's integration capabilities support sophisticated workflows through connections with: E-commerce platforms for automated sales recording Inventory management systems for real-time stock tracking Customer relationship management tools for unified client views Payroll services for streamlined employee compensation QuickBooks' developer-friendly architecture encourages continuous expansion of integration options. New applications regularly join the ecosystem, ensuring businesses can connect with emerging technologies and specialized services as their needs evolve. This forward-looking approach helps future-proof your accounting infrastructure. Xero's Cloud-First Integration Approach Xero's cloud-based architecture facilitates seamless integration with thousands of third-party applications. The platform's API-first design philosophy prioritizes connectivity, allowing for robust data exchange between systems without compromising security or performance. This approach creates a flexible foundation for building customized business management solutions. The platform excels particularly in e-commerce and inventory integrations, offering specialized connections with platforms like Shopify, Amazon, and dedicated inventory management systems. These integrations automatically synchronize sales data, inventory levels, and customer information, creating a unified system that reduces manual reconciliation work. Xero continues advancing its integration capabilities through artificial intelligence features that enhance automation. Bank reconciliation predictions and cash flow analytics tools leverage machine learning to identify patterns and suggest actions, further streamlining financial management processes. These AI-powered features represent the cutting edge of accounting software innovation. How To Choose The Right Accounting Software Selecting the ideal accounting platform requires careful consideration of your specific business requirements, technical capabilities, and growth trajectory. The perfect solution balances functionality against usability while providing room for expansion as your business evolves. Take advantage of free trials offered by each platform to experience their interfaces and workflows firsthand. Practical testing reveals usability factors that specifications alone cannot convey and helps identify which system best matches your working style. Assess Your Business Requirements First Start by evaluating your current business size and anticipated growth trajectory. Freelancers and micro-businesses with simple financial structures might find FreshBooks perfectly adequate, while rapidly growing companies or those with complex accounting needs might benefit from QuickBooks or Xero's more robust capabilities. Consider which specific accounting functions matter most to your operation. If invoicing, expense tracking, and time management represent your core requirements, FreshBooks provides these essentials with exceptional ease of use. For businesses needing detailed reporting, inventory management, or multi-user collaboration, QuickBooks or Xero offer more comprehensive solutions. Your technical comfort level should influence your decision significantly. FreshBooks prioritizes intuitive design for non-accountants, while QuickBooks and Xero deliver more advanced capabilities with correspondingly steeper learning curves. Be realistic about how much time you can dedicate to learning a new system and whether you have accounting expertise available internally. Evaluate Integration Requirements Carefully Identify which other business applications must connect with your accounting system. Common integration needs include: E-commerce platforms for online sales businesses Project management tools for service-based companies Inventory systems for product-based operations CRM software for sales-focused organizations Consider both current and anticipated future integration requirements when evaluating platforms. While all three options offer integration capabilities, QuickBooks and Xero provide substantially larger ecosystems that accommodate specialized and emerging technologies. This expanded connectivity becomes increasingly valuable as your business grows and diversifies. Determine how automated you want your financial processes to be. Greater automation reduces manual data entry but requires more sophisticated integrations between systems. Platforms with robust API capabilities like Xero and QuickBooks typically offer more advanced automation possibilities than simpler systems focused primarily on ease of use. Consider Long-Term Value Beyond Initial Price Evaluate pricing structures in relation to your specific usage patterns. FreshBooks typically offers better value for freelancers and very small businesses with basic needs, while QuickBooks pricing increases more substantially as you add features and users. Xero's unlimited user model provides excellent value for businesses with multiple team members requiring system access. Factor in potential hidden costs beyond the monthly subscription fee. Additional expenses might include: Per-user access fees for team members or accountants Transaction fees for payment processing Add-on costs for specialized features like payroll Implementation and training expenses for complex systems Consider the long-term value proposition rather than focusing exclusively on initial costs. A slightly more expensive platform that grows with your business might ultimately provide better value than a cheaper option you'll outgrow quickly. Evaluate each system's scalability against your business's projected growth trajectory when assessing overall value. Maximize Your Accounting Software Investment Implementing accounting software represents just the beginning of your financial management journey. Getting the most value from your chosen platform requires thoughtful setup, regular maintenance, and strategic utilization of available features. Proper implementation establishes a solid foundation for financial accuracy and efficiency. Taking time to configure your system correctly from the start prevents costly errors and rework later. Consider working with an implementation specialist if you're adopting a complex platform like QuickBooks or Xero. Optimize Your Setup Process Begin with a comprehensive chart of accounts tailored to your specific business needs. This fundamental structure determines how financial transactions get categorized and reported. Consider consulting with an accountant to ensure your chart of accounts supports both operational needs and tax reporting requirements. Import historical financial data carefully to establish accurate baselines. Most platforms offer tools to import bank transactions, customer records, and vendor information from previous systems. Verify this imported data thoroughly before proceeding with new transactions to ensure continuity in your financial records. Configure user permissions appropriately if multiple team members will access the system. Establish clear boundaries between viewing, editing, and administrative privileges based on each user's role and responsibilities. This security approach protects sensitive financial information while enabling necessary collaboration. Implement Best Financial Practices Follow these proven strategies to maximize accounting software benefits: Reconcile accounts regularly, ideally weekly or monthly, to catch discrepancies early and maintain accurate financial records. Create standardized processes for recurring financial tasks like invoicing, expense approval, and payment processing to ensure consistency. Establish clear documentation for financial procedures that anyone in your organization can follow if primary users are unavailable. Schedule regular financial reviews using the reporting tools in your accounting platform to identify trends and address issues proactively. Keep your software updated to access new features, security improvements, and bug fixes that enhance performance. Leverage automation capabilities to reduce manual work and minimize errors. Set up recurring invoices for subscription clients, automatic payment reminders for overdue accounts, and scheduled reports for regular financial reviews. These automated processes free up time for more strategic financial management activities. Continuously Improve Your Financial Systems Schedule periodic reviews of your accounting system to identify improvement opportunities. As your business evolves, your financial management needs will change accordingly. Regular assessments ensure your accounting platform continues to serve your requirements effectively. Consider working with an accounting professional who specializes in your chosen platform. Their expertise can help you discover advanced features, optimize workflows, and implement best practices specific to your industry. This professional guidance often delivers substantial efficiency improvements that justify the consulting investment. Stay informed about new features and updates released for your accounting platform. Vendors regularly enhance their software with additional capabilities that might address challenges you're currently facing. Following the platform's blog, attending webinars, or joining user communities helps you stay current with these developments. Transform Your Financial Management Today Selecting the right accounting software fundamentally transforms how you manage your business finances. The perfect platform streamlines daily operations, provides valuable insights, and scales alongside your growing enterprise. Your choice between Xero, QuickBooks, and FreshBooks should align with your specific business requirements, technical capabilities, and growth trajectory. Each platform offers distinct advantages for different business profiles. FreshBooks delivers exceptional simplicity and focused functionality ideal for freelancers and very small businesses. QuickBooks provides comprehensive capabilities and extensive integrations perfect for established companies with complex accounting needs. Xero combines modern design with powerful features and unlimited user access, making it excellent for collaborative teams and growing businesses. Take advantage of free trials to experience each platform firsthand before committing. These trial periods allow you to test workflows, explore features, and evaluate usability in your specific business context. Consult with your accountant or financial advisor during this evaluation process to ensure your chosen platform supports both operational needs and compliance requirements. With the right accounting software in place, you'll gain greater financial clarity, improved operational efficiency, and stronger foundations for sustainable business growth.

title: What Neptune Got Right (And How to Keep It)
summary: Neptune is shutting down on March 5, 2026 (10am PST). For teams that have been using it for years, the real loss isn't just the migration work. It's losing one of the few trackers that stayed fast when projects got big.
body_text: Neptune is shutting down on March 5, 2026 (10am PST). For teams that have been using it for years, the real loss isn't just the migration work. It's losing one of the few trackers that stayed fast when projects got big. At Trainy , we build infrastructure for GPU clusters. When the shutdown was announced, our customers started asking what they should migrate to. The recurring requirement wasn't "more features", it was responsiveness with thousands of runs and heavy time-series logging. That's what Neptune consistently nailed, and none of the alternatives our customers evaluated matched it. So we built Pluto : an experiment tracker based on our fork of the open source project MLOp . Same focus on staying snappy at scale, with a low-risk migration path. Dual-log by adding one import, validate parity, then cut over when you're ready. This post is about what made Neptune good, what we think could be better, and how we approached building Pluto. What Neptune Got Right Scalability and responsiveness Neptune handled scale well. You could log 50k+ metrics per run with no dropped points and no timeouts under sustained logging. Projects with thousands of runs remained usable. And the UI was fast: graphs loaded quickly, filtering the runs table didn't freeze the page. This sounds basic, but if you've used a slow experiment tracker while trying to debug a training run, you know how much it matters. The query system Neptune's query language (NQL) was actually quite powerful. You could filter runs by any field: recall > 0.9 AND learning_rate <= 0.005 . You could combine conditions with AND/OR, use comparison operators on metrics, filter by tags, owners, dates. The query builder made it easy to construct these without memorizing syntax. Side-by-side comparison Neptune's side-by-side view was well designed. It stacked attributes as rows instead of columns, which made scrolling through differences easier. You could filter to show only rows with differences, set a reference run to see relative changes, and even diff long strings character-by-character. Where We See Room to Build Graph UX Neptune's graphing was solid, but there were a few areas where we think the experience could be better: Legend sorting was based on current metric value, which meant the order shifted as you scrubbed through time Filtering views within graphs required manually hiding metrics one by one Smoothing was global rather than per-panel or per-metric Syncing axes across graphs for debugging gradient spikes required manual axis linking per chart group Dev Workflow Neptune lived somewhat separately from the rest of your workflow. We'd want the ability to tie experiments to Linear/Jira issues, terminate running jobs from the UI, and view code diffs in the UI. That last one came up a lot for us: two runs, identical hyperparameters, different results. Something in the code changed, but you'd have to track down git commits and diff them yourself. Tensor logging Neptune required you to render plots client-side before logging them. There was no way to natively plot raw tensors on the fly. Logging tensors directly and generating visualizations server-side would let teams iterate on what they visualize without worrying about rendering and saving images client-side. LLM Integration Experiment data is a natural fit for LLM querying. Being able to ask "which runs last week had the lowest validation loss" or get automatic summaries of experiment batches would save a lot of manual dashboard digging. (We shipped an early version of this with Pluto MCP , currently in alpha.) Pluto's Stack Pluto is built with the same focus on responsiveness that made Neptune good. It's based on our fork of MLOp , and we've been working with design partners to figure out what actually matters to teams running serious training workloads. Under the hood: ClickHouse for OLAP, enabling fast analytics on metric series with 1M+ points. Postgres OLTP for user, organization, and run metadata. Rust ingestion server for fast non-blocking metric writes. We added on-disk buffering to both the client and server for increased reliability against networking hiccups. Ingestion server handles 2000+ req/s end-to-end per replica. P95 latency: 200ms at 2k req/s. React frontend for a responsive UX. We added lazy loading optimizations to increase the responsiveness of the UI even when multiple runs and charts are being loaded on a single page. Whole stack is self-hostable via docker-compose in about a minute. While we host this stack with multiple replicas for high availability, it's still very fast on a single machine with around 8 CPUs, 32GB RAM, and 1TB disk. Neptune compatibility layer We built a compatibility layer so you can dual-log to both Neptune and Pluto with minimal code changes: import pluto.compat.neptune # Add this line from neptune_scale import Run # Your existing Neptune Scale import # Your existing Neptune Scale code works unchanged run = Run(experiment_name="my-experiment") run.log_configs({"lr": 0.001, "batch_size": 32}) run.log_metrics({"train/loss": 0.5}, step=0) run.close() Set the PLUTO_PROJECT environment variable and your metrics log to both platforms. This is intentional. We wanted to eliminate all risk of trying Pluto. Your Neptune logging keeps working exactly as before. If Pluto breaks, you still have Neptune. If you don't like Pluto, remove the import and nothing changes. There's no commitment until you're ready. When you are ready to stop logging to Neptune entirely: export DISABLE_NEPTUNE_LOGGING=true All Neptune API calls get redirected to Pluto. No code changes required. Migration Guide Common pitfalls Before diving in, a few things worth knowing: Exports take longer than you'd expect. Neptune explicitly warns that workspace exports can take days to weeks depending on size. Don't wait until the last week of February. Artifact sizes and storage planning. If you've been logging model checkpoints, large files, or images, figure out how much storage you'll need on the other side before you start. Legacy Neptune client vs Neptune Scale. Pluto's compatibility layer targets Neptune Scale ( neptune-scale package), not the legacy neptune client. If your codebase still uses the old client, you'll need to migrate to Neptune Scale first. Run IDs and fork mapping. Neptune's internal run IDs and fork relationships don't have a universal standard. Make sure your export preserves the lineage you care about. Verifying parity means more than metrics. When we say "validate that everything matches," that includes step counts, tags, system metrics, and logged files, not just the loss curves. Step 1: Set up dual-logging Add the compatibility import and set the PLUTO_PROJECT environment variable as described in the compatibility layer section above. Run this on real training workloads to validate at scale. Step 2: Export your Neptune history We have an exporter that brings your historical runs into Pluto. Details: Exporting Neptune Runs Step 3: Validate and give us feedback Before removing Neptune: Do metrics match between both platforms? Is the UI responsive at your scale? Can your team find what they need? This is where we need your help. If something's missing, broken, or would block your migration, tell us. Email roanak@trainy.ai or open an issue on GitHub. We're shipping fixes fast and your feedback directly shapes what we build next. Step 4: Cut over Set DISABLE_NEPTUNE_LOGGING=true . All Neptune calls redirect to Pluto. Done. Pricing and Links Pluto's hosted plan is $250/seat/month, matching Neptune's pricing. Live playground , no signup required Quickstart Neptune migration docs GitHub We're listed on Neptune's official transition hub . Pluto is open-source. The Python client is Apache-2.0 licensed. The server is AGPL-3.0. You can self-host the entire stack via docker-compose: clone the server repo, copy .env.example to .env , and run docker compose up --build . The server README has full setup instructions. Questions? Email roanak@trainy.ai or book a time .

body_text: RBI Reaffirms Growth Algorithm, including 8%+ Organic Adjusted Operating Income Growth and 5%+ Net Restaurant Growth by 2028, with Plans to Return $1.6 Billion of Capital to Shareholders in 2026 Company Release - 2/26/2026 8:00 AM ET Download the PDF version PDF Format (opens in new window) MIAMI , Feb. 26, 2026 /CNW/ - Restaurant Brands International Inc. ("RBI", "Company") (NYSE: QSR) (TSX: QSR) (TSX: QSP) today hosted its 2026 Investor Day at the Company's Miami headquarters, reaffirming expectations to deliver against its growth algorithm within the 2028 outlook period and providing enhanced visibility into the execution of its strategic plan. The Company also announced plans to return over $1.6 billion of capital to shareholders in 2026 through both dividends and the resumption of share repurchases. KEY HIGHLIGHTS: Reaffirmed 8%+ organic Adjusted Operating Income growth from 2024-2028; having delivered over 8% in both 2024 and 2025 Provided a path to 5%+ Net Restaurant Growth by 2028, with distinct building blocks adding visibility and confidence in plans Announced that the majority of excess free cash flow will be earmarked for share repurchases, commencing with $500 million in 2026 Unveiled goal of becoming an investment-grade company and expectations to achieve corporate investment-grade leverage by 2028 Outlined simplification roadmap including intent to sunset Restaurant Holdings segment by the end of 2027 Updated long-term capital spending framework with capital expenditures, tenant inducements, and incentives ("Capex and Cash Inducements") declining to roughly $300 million annually from 2028 onward President of Burger King US and Canada, Tom Curtis, announced extension of elevated 4.5% franchisee advertising fund contribution rate through at least 2027 and provided details on accelerating momentum of the Reclaim the Flame plan "We are building a simpler, stronger, and more focused RBI – a world-class restaurant company designed to win for decades. Our growth is powered by four iconic brands with deep heritage in their communities and enduring guest loyalty, supported by exceptional franchisees and great talent around the world," said Josh Kobza, Chief Executive Officer of RBI. "As we look toward 2028 and beyond, we see a highly franchised, asset-light business delivering consistent 5%+ Net Restaurant Growth, predictable earnings growth, and strong double-digit total shareholder returns. The strength of our brands and the quality of our teams position us to compound value for all our stakeholders for many years to come." Sami Siddiqui, Chief Financial Officer, commented: "We're committed to becoming a simpler, 99% franchised business over the next few years. Our business generates significant free cash flow, which gives us substantial capital allocation flexibility. We've always prioritized investing in our brands, maintaining a strong balance sheet, and returning excess cash to shareholders through our attractive dividend. We're resuming share repurchases in 2026, and we've made the decision to become an investment-grade company. We believe we're only two years away from achieving corporate investment-grade leverage, which, once achieved, will unlock meaningful long-term flexibility for our business." Patrick Doyle, Executive Chairman, commented: "When I invested in RBI three years ago, I saw a company with great brands, great food, great people, and great franchisees executing the fundamentals that drive long-term success in this business. Today, we're delivering on exactly what attracted me to invest in this company. RBI continues to make the right long-term decisions for the business. We allocate capital well and keep franchisee profitability at the center of our decision-making. I cannot imagine a more exciting time to be part of the RBI story." CLEAR PATH TO 5%+ NET RESTAURANT GROWTH RBI outlined three building blocks to achieve 5%+ Net Restaurant Growth by 2028, representing approximately 1,800 net new restaurants per year by 2028. Outside of Burger King China, RBI's Net Restaurant Growth has averaged 4.0% over the past five years, underscoring the strength and diversity of the core development engine. US and Canada (300-400 net new restaurants per year by 2028): Growth in the US and Canada is expected to be driven by Firehouse Subs, Tim Hortons, and Popeyes. Firehouse Subs is expected to contribute approximately half of the net new units in the US and Canada, with 150-200 net new units per year, driven by improving brand awareness and strong unit economics, with paybacks under four years, on average. The remaining 150-200 net new units will be roughly split between Tim Hortons and Popeyes. Tim Hortons Canada growth is supported by opportunities in underpenetrated regions including Western Canada and Quebec, as well as attractive paybacks, which are less than three years on average. In the US, the team is on track to continue accelerating development in both existing and new markets, like Virginia, Florida, Delaware, Tennessee, New York, Michigan, New Jersey, and Texas. While Popeyes tempered development in 2025, the team is laying the operational groundwork to position the brand to reaccelerate in the years ahead. China (300-400 net new restaurants per year by 2028): Burger King China's partnership with CPE, announced in November 2025, is on track to deliver over 200 net new units in 2028, with continued acceleration after 2028, as CPE executes on its commitment to double the brand's footprint to 2,500 restaurants within five years. CPE's $350 million primary capital investment is intended to fully fund this development. Popeyes China and Tim Hortons China are expected to contribute the remaining 100-200 combined net new units in 2028 as both businesses scale. International Excluding China (approximately 1,100 net new restaurants per year by 2028): Top 10 growth markets including India, the UK, Mexico, France, and Japan are expected to deliver approximately 700 units per year by 2028, supported by strong unit economics, with paybacks under four and a half years, on average. The remaining international portfolio of around 175 brand-market combinations are expected to contribute approximately 400 new units per year. BURGER KING RECLAIM THE FLAME GROWTH STRATEGY DELIVERING RESULTS Tom Curtis, President of Burger King US and Canada, provided an update on Reclaim the Flame , the brand's comprehensive growth strategy, which has delivered four years of burger QSR industry Comparable Sales outperformance since launching in 2022. The brand has moved from 10th to 6th place in industry guest experience rankings, increased modern image penetration from 37% in 2021 to 58% in 2025, and improved franchisee profitability from a low of around $125,000 to approximately $205,000 in both 2023 and 2024. Looking through the impact of temporary beef inflation and ad fund transfers, franchisee profitability grew in 2025, demonstrating that actions within the brand's control are working to expand profitability even during a challenging environment. In addition, Burger King franchisees have voted to continue their elevated ad fund contribution of 4.5% of sales through at least 2027, with 97% voting to support the continued advertising firepower. The ad fund rate will continue at this level in 2028 if the business achieves $230,000 in franchisee profitability by the end of 2027 or if the franchisees vote to extend again. This continued investment supports sustained marketing share of voice and demonstrates strong franchisee confidence in the brand's trajectory. Looking ahead, Burger King will elevate culinary quality, beginning with enhancements to the Whopper, including new glazed buns, creamier mayonnaise, and upgraded clamshell packaging. In 2026, the brand will also launch a major campaign reinforcing its commitment to listening to and acting on guest feedback. Additionally, Burger King sees meaningful opportunity to win with families and kids, who represent just 10% of the brand's traffic today. The Company also introduced BK Assistant, an AI-powered tool designed to streamline restaurant operations by providing managers and team members with instant access to operational guidelines, inventory management, and compliance tracking, enabling them to focus more on guest service and team leadership. SIMPLIFICATION ROADMAP AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION UPDATE Sami Siddiqui, Chief Financial Officer, outlined RBI's simplification roadmap and enhanced capital allocation framework, and emphasized the transition to a 99% franchised model, corporate investment-grade leverage by 2028, and resumption of share repurchases, with around $500 million expected in 2026. Share repurchases are expected to grow over time as the Company uses the majority of annual excess free cash flow for buybacks, with capacity to accelerate further once investment grade is achieved. In addition, RBI committed to its durable and growing dividend, with a long-term target payout ratio of around 60%.
